title: Behaviour module manifest
description: What a behaviour module declares, checked when a world loads (docs/design/rebuild.md 5.2): its parameters (types, units, ranges, and each figure's source or that it's a placeholder), what it relies on perceiving, the beliefs it keeps (for truth audits), the decisions it records, and that its state can be saved (for checkpoints). A world that doesn't give a module what it declares is refused at load, naming the module.

name.description: As worlds name it in controller.impl, e.g. citizen.default.

doc.description: Where its rules are documented, with their sources.

perceives.description: What it relies on perceiving: the seat's channels must provide each.

answers.description: How the office answers a letter: its name in words, what it acts on (the sentence it sends after its report or acknowledgement), whether it has a standing report of its own, and, where a letter plainly concerns something it has a form for, what it says of that (docs/behaviour/letters.md).

capacity.description: What sizes the office's staff, where the engine's kind states it: its asks per thousand residents a year, the seconds one answer takes, the rule that sizes the staff, and the figure's source and reason (docs/behaviour/staffing.md).

beliefs.description: Beliefs it reports each wake for truth audits (docs/design/rebuild.md 8.2).

decisions.description: Domains of the decisions it records.

state.description: Whether it saves and restores its state, for resuming from a checkpoint.

keeps.description: Whole collections its seats are shown unasked because this is the office that keeps them (the land registry its register, a bank its customers' instructions), each with the reason. Nobody is shown a whole register, population or map unless its module says so here (docs/no-god-view.md).

boundary.description: What it carries of the world's edge: boundary conditions of the simulation it is handed (the weather to come, the outside market's scripted prices), each with the reason (docs/no-god-view.md).

takes.description: The written directions its office takes (docs/behaviour/directions.md): for each, the form the office publishes for it and what following one means. A direction is followed only when it is filed on the form by someone the office's organisation says may direct it (a record of the world's, never this manifest), from the office's next plan until it is replaced or withdrawn. A world publishes one form for each, from this declaration.

routines.description: The routine tasks its office's staff do by standing work order (docs/behaviour/standing-work.md; contracts/calls.md, a standing work order): for each, the task's name as an order names it, what doing it is, in words, and which parameter says where it is done. Where a model holds the office, a world gives the office's staff a post of their own, run by this module, which does a routine only while a standing order of the organisation's is in force for it; the office-holder sets the orders.

at.description: The parameter that holds the place the work is done at.

every.description: The routine's own rhythm, where the office's practice has one: days, or the parameter that gives them with what it is where none is given. Said in the office's procedure; a standing work order that does not say how often follows it.

papers.description: For a routine whose task is `answer` (the counter): the kinds of incoming paper the office's counter staff sort and answer under the office's procedure, and, in plain words, how. Such a paper does not bring the office-holder back, and reaches them as a count and a sample; anything addressed to the office-holder's own post by name, or resting on a paper they made themself, reaches them whatever its kind (docs/behaviour/standing-work.md, the counter).

follows.description: Where when the routine is done is set by a published paper and not by a rhythm (a rating law's instalments): the parameter that names the paper, with the paper where none is given. A standing work order may name it in place of how often, or say nothing.

issues.description: The papers its office issues, each as a form of the office's own stationery (docs/behaviour/office-papers.md): the form's fields, and how they are written into the statement the rest of the world reads (outcomes.schema.json, FormWrites). In `writes`, a string "@name" stands for something of the office's own that a world fills in when it publishes the form. A world publishes these for an office a model holds; filled in, each makes the paper the module itself makes.

does.description: What issuing the paper does, for whoever holds the office: said on the form with its name. A sentence; or, for a paper that is a step of a procedure a law sets (a notice to vacate, an order for possession), a few: what it does, what it does not do by itself, and where what the law asks before it is written.

form.description: The form's name, as the call language's form names it.

title.description: What the form is, in a few words.

fields.description: The form's fields, as a form's data has them (outcomes.schema.json, FormData).

follows.description: What following it means, in words: what the office does while the direction stands.

schema.description: A JSON Schema for its value.

unit.description: e.g. cents, bps, days, seconds, count.

required.description: The world must give it (whom a module deals with, a place's figures).

source.description: Where the default figure comes from; 'placeholder' when it's unsourced.

what.description: A statement kind (enrolment), a record type (records:claim), directory, map, every entity of a kind (every:factory), or future.

why.description: Why this kind of participant holds it whole, in words.

about.description: What in the world it's checked against.
